claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. My son Alex - he's 19 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand his current situation a bit better.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he enrolled in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications at school or college)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. I need to understand a bit more about his education to properly assess eligibility.

**Is Alex enrolled in full-time education at the sixth form college?** (This typically means more than 12 hours per week of supervised study or course-related work experience.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's doing full-time A-levels - so he's there most weekdays with all his classes and coursework.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, that's very helpful information. Now I need to clarify one more important detail about his education:

**When did Alex turn 19?** Specifically, I need to know if he turned 19 before or after 31 August (the start of the current academic year), or if his 19th birthday is still coming up.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 19 before the start of September - so before the current academic year started.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 19 years old
- He turned 19 before the start of the current academic year (before 31 August/early September)
- He is in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels at sixth form college)

Unfortunately, this means that Child Benefit eligibility for Alex would have ended. The rules state that Child Benefit continues for young people in approved education or training only until they turn 20, **or until 31 August following their 19th birthday, whichever comes first**. Since Alex turned 19 before the start of the academic year (before 31 August), his eligibility would have ended on 31 August following his 19th birthday.

Let me provide you with the formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. While he is continuing his education, which is positive, the age limit rules mean that Child Benefit stops on 31 August after a young person turns 19, even if they remain in education.

If you have any questions about this decision or need further clarification, please let me know.
